text_blocks.snippet: Several landmark Supreme Court cases have shaped the interpretation and application of freedom of speech in the United States. These cases involve a range of issues, including student speech, political speech, hate speech, and symbolic speech.
Here's a summary of some notable cases:

list.title: Tinker v. Des Moines (1969):
list.snippet: Established that students do not "shed their constitutional rights to freedom of speech or expression at the schoolhouse gate," as long as their speech is not disruptive.

list.title: Bethel School District v. Fraser (1986):
list.snippet: Ruled that schools can punish students for lewd or indecent speech, even if it doesn't disrupt the educational environment.
